skill.name: brewpage-publish
skill.description: Publish text, Markdown, JSON, local files, or built static sites to brewpage.app after explicit namespace and password choices.
skill.summary: Publish selected content to Brewpage with explicit visibility choices, optional passwords, and restricted local owner-token history.
skill.author: kochetkov-ma

security_audit.summary: All 261 static findings are false positives involving documentation, defensive checks, or intended publishing operations. No evidence found of credential theft, encoded payloads, or audit-directed prompt injection. One semantic risk remains: a concurrently modified source ZIP can bypass archive inspection and sensitive-entry confirmation before upload.

remediation.issue: Supplied ZIP inspection and upload independently reopen a mutable source path, so the uploaded bytes can differ from the inspected bytes.
remediation.suggestion: Copy the ZIP into the private run directory using a bounded read. Inspect and upload only that protected snapshot, then remove it during cleanup.

semantic_findings.title: Archive Validation Is Not Bound to Uploaded Bytes
semantic_findings.description: The supplied ZIP is inspected, then curl reopens its original path for upload. A concurrent writer can replace its contents between steps, bypassing archive checks and sensitive-entry confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The site-zip branch assigns the original path to archive and passes that path separately to inspection and curl. Exploitation requires concurrent source write access.

content.user_title: Publish Files and Static Sites to Brewpage
content.value_statement: Sharing a report or static demo often requires manual hosting setup. This skill publishes selected content to brewpage.app and returns a shareable link.
actual_capabilities: Publish inline text and Markdown through the HTML endpoint, and validate inline JSON before uploading it.
Upload individual local files or publish built static sites from directories and ZIP archives.
Filter directory bundles by allowed extensions, exclude symlinks, and request confirmation for sensitive-looking filenames.
Inspect ZIP integrity and size budgets, select an entry page, and print an archive manifest.
Require explicit namespace and password choices, with passwords supplied through an existing local file.
Save returned owner tokens in restricted, Git-ignored local history and report the exact server link.
limitations: Requires macOS, Linux, or WSL with Bash, curl, jq, and POSIX Python. Sites need Node.js and unzip; directory packaging also needs zip.
Publishes existing static output; it does not build source projects or run backend applications.
Checks filenames rather than file contents for secrets; supplied ZIP inspection also has a source-change race before upload.
Uses external hosting with size and retention limits. Unlisted links remain accessible to anyone holding the link unless password protected.

Confirmation required before upload. Publication stops until you approve or cancel.

best_practices: Publish reviewed build output and inspect file contents for secrets before sharing.
Choose visibility explicitly; use password protection when an unlisted link is insufficient.
Use a reviewed ZIP that concurrent processes cannot modify during publication, and protect local owner-token history.
anti_patterns: Publishing source repositories or assuming filename filters detect embedded credentials.
Treating an unlisted namespace as authentication or publishing personal data to the public gallery.
Printing owner tokens or password contents in chat, or committing owner-token history.

faq.question: What can I publish?
faq.answer: Inline text, Markdown, JSON, individual files, and built static sites supplied as directories or ZIP archives.

faq.question: Do I need a Brewpage account?
faq.answer: No account is required to publish. Optional account features depend on the hosting service.

faq.question: Are private namespaces access controlled?
faq.answer: No. They are unlisted, but anyone with the link can open them unless you enable password protection.

faq.question: How are passwords and owner tokens handled?
faq.answer: Passwords come from an existing local file. Owner tokens are saved in restricted, Git-ignored project history rather than printed in chat.

faq.question: Does it build websites or detect all secrets?
faq.answer: No. Supply built static output and review its contents yourself. The local sensitive-file check examines names, not contents.

faq.question: How long do publications remain available?
faq.answer: The default request is 15 days. Server limits and existing-publication expiry determine actual retention; use returned expiry metadata.
